subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: How should strict outbound sanitization handle an unclosed `<think>` block when a `<final>` opener appears inside the same text payload?
rationale: The code can either recover visible answer text or suppress malformed payloads, but that choice affects hidden-reasoning exposure and message-loss behavior across channels.

options.title: Recover final text safely
options.body: Parse the original malformed payload for a `<final>` body before stripping markers, drop the hidden reasoning, and add channel regression proof.

options.title: Suppress malformed strict payloads
options.body: Treat unclosed thinking in strict mode as unsafe and deliver nothing unless a later well-formed final answer arrives.

options.title: Defer until live repro
options.body: Keep the current fallback while collecting a current WhatsApp or Telegram live reproduction to calibrate the security/message-loss tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Recover final text safely
recommendation.body: Parse the original malformed payload for a `<final>` body before stripping markers, drop the hidden reasoning, and add channel regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on shared assistant-visible sanitizer semantics, where this history shows the strongest ownership signal.
